scenes.text: And at night, I dreamed in green. [pause] Black screens, glowing green lines, like <emphasis>Tron</emphasis>. AND gates, XOR gates, NAND gates, waiting to be burned into a chip.

Fair warning. [pause] This is an embellished fictional dramatization that <emphasis>may or may not</emphasis> be based on true stories. The narrator is a guy named Charlie Hack, and any resemblance to me is mostly coincidental. Names, characters, companies and events are fictitious, or used fictitiously.
<emphasis>All three of us</emphasis> had the same dream. Real life bled into our dreams.
Silicon Valley is very good at telling a story about A players. The people who look like they were always going to win, and the companies that look like they were always going to work.
scenes.tts: Silicon Valley is very good at telling a story about A-players. The people who look like they were always going to win, and the companies that look like they were always going to work.

scenes.text: The myth is a straight line: a garage, a genius, a ticker symbol. But most of the real work looks like another ordinary Tuesday.

And from the outside, a C thing can look like an A thing. [pause] A C player is not a failure. It's the person who was never the smartest in the room, and kept going anyway. [pause] Because there is always the smarter guy in the room.
Good at everything beats best at one thing. That's a C player.
The Valley falls in love with products. I got more out of building a <emphasis>platform</emphasis>: a foundation you can stand on, then build the next thing on.
You stack building blocks: habits, fundamentals, the unglamorous layer nobody puts on a slide. [pause] That layer is what you actually stand on later.

The gymnastics foundation is the hollow hold, just on the ground. Virtuosity in something as simple as a hollow hold is what makes the next layer easy. Fundamentals, then building blocks, then intensity.
I had one opportunity that year, and twenty weeks of training before it. There is a golden rule: nothing new on race day. Why am I calm, cool, collected? Because it's just another Saturday.
Then the work itself changed. [pause] I'm usually the most excited person in the room about A.I. Which is funny, because I should be the <emphasis>saddest</emphasis>.

Because A.I. came after the code writers first. [pause] In my own work, A.I. now writes essentially all of the code I ship. That's how I work. Not a measured team result. Not a general industry figure.
Most companies strive for well. I strive for fit. [pause] A.I. is even more powerful to those that actually understand the fundamentals.

Greg Glassman noticed that the fittest person on earth might rank only in the 75th percentile at any single event. Good at everything beats best at one thing. [pause] C players are good and strong fundamentally in multiple areas, and ultimately that's what makes them a winner. [pause] That's the whole point of this book. The 75th-percentile C player who stacks fundamentals across many areas beats the A player who is best at just one thing.

scenes.text: The book begins with that green-screen dream. It ends by dreaming about A.I. [pause] It's free. It's open. The story is still being written.
More chapters are coming. [pause] And when version one is ready, if you were around for any of it, you get to tell your side.
Silicon Valley C Players. Coming in 2027.
